A 54-year-old female patient presents with a 2-day history of intense neck pain that began after
abruptly twisting her neck while reaching for an item on a high shelf. Her medical history includes
hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. She works as a librarian, frequently performing tasks that
require overhead reaching. She drinks one glass of wine per week and denies smoking. Her body
mass index is 24 kg/m², and her vital signs are within normal limits. On physical examination, C6 shows
restricted left rotation that improves with backward bending of the head. When treating this patient's
somatic dysfunction using the high velocity, low amplitude (HVLA) technique, what is the correct
approach? Answer Choices: (A) apply a rotational thrust directed toward the ipsilateral eye (B) apply a
posterior thrust directed along the cervical spine axis (C) apply a sidebending thrust directed toward the
ipsilateral shoulder (D) position C6 into right rotation and apply a downward thrust (E) position C6 into
left translation before applying a thrust (F) position C6 into right translation before applying a thrust (G)
ask the patient to flex the neck before applying a thrust (H) position the cervical spine into flexion and
apply a rotational thrust (I) apply a sidebending thrust directed toward the contralateral shoulder (J) use
a lateral translation thrust directed toward the contralateral side
 A. apply a sidebending thrust directed toward the ipsilateral shoulder
B. ask the patient to flex the neck before applying a thrust
C. position the cervical spine into flexion and apply a rotational thrust
D. apply a sidebending thrust directed toward the contralateral shoulder
E. position C6 into left translation before applying a thrust
F. apply a posterior thrust directed along the cervical spine axis
G. apply a rotational thrust directed toward the ipsilateral eye
H. position C6 into right translation before applying a thrust
I. use a lateral translation thrust directed toward the contralateral side
J. position C6 into right rotation and apply a downward thrust
